transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-02-18 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Claire (Redwood AE), Darren (Redwood SE), Priya (Midnight Energy - Head of Platform), Marcelo (ML Eng), Aisha (Security)

Summary: Quick discovery to validate fit for Redwood hosted API as a PLG onramp; discuss free credits and how fast they can get to first token; surface security/compliance needs to decide between hosted vs dedicated/private.

[00:00] Claire: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Claire, account lead at Redwood Inference, and with me is Darren, our solutions engineer. How's the audio for folks?
[00:12] Priya: Good here, thanks. Excited to chat, we've been poking at different inference providers.
[00:16] Marcelo: Audio good.
[00:18] Aisha: All good.

[00:22] Claire: Great. High level agenda — first, quick understanding of your current stack and goals; second, walk through our PLG/self-serve quickstart and free credits model — basically how fast you can go from signup to a first token; third, hosted vs dedicated vs private considerations given security; and last, next steps and benchmarks. Sound ok?
[00:38] Priya: Yep, sounds perfect. For context: Midnight Energy is building an internal assistant for operators and a customer-facing energy-cost-optimizer. We're evaluating inference backends for embeddings, chat and a small reranker. Important constraints: P95 latency under 400ms for customer flows, SOC2 compliance, and some EU data residency rules.
[01:05] Claire: That's helpful — thanks. Quick question on scale: Marcelo, what are you seeing for qps on the customer-facing path and expected token lengths?
[01:14] Marcelo: Right now PoC traffic is low, maybe 10–20 qps max, but if we launch regionally could spike to 200 qps during peak. Token lengths vary — typical prompts 80–200 tokens, responses 50–300 tokens.
[01:30] Darren: Ok that's a helpful shape. With that traffic profile you can start on hosted and typically we can route you to our standard low-latency models. If you need predictable tails or dedicated GPUs for consistent throughput, Redwood Dedicated is the next step. For strict data residency or air-gapped regs, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is the option.

[01:54] Priya: I guess our first priority is getting something in prod fast via self-serve. We liked the idea of free credits and a sandbox. How fast is time-to-first-token realistically?
[02:05] Claire: For a developer who signs up and uses the SDK: median time-to-first-token is under 10 minutes — often 2–5 minutes if you have no network/firewall blockers. We provide a quickstart repo and a template that shows a curl call, plus SDK snippets for Node/Python. We'll also pre-populate a trial org with credits so you can immediately run inference.

[02:27] Marcelo: Any gotchas? We've had issues before where keys are blocked by corp firewall or the SDK expects certain TLS ciphers.
[02:35] Darren: Good note. Usually firewall and egress rules are the main friction. Our quickstart runbook includes endpoints, and if you need private endpoints we can enable VPC endpoints for trial customers but that adds setup. For most teams, the hosted public API works fine. We'll include a troubleshooting section in the runbook.

[02:54] Aisha: Security question — we have to demonstrate SOC 2 compliance and SSO via SAML. How does Redwood handle log retention and KMS?
[03:03] Claire: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — we'll send the report. We support SAML/SSO + SCIM for provisioning. For encryption, customers can use our managed keys or integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for hosted we provide encryption at rest and in transit with audit logs available. We'll share the security datasheet and the compliance pack.

[03:28] Priya: What about data residency for EU customers? We need requests to be processed within the EU region.
[03:35] Darren: We have region routing; you can pin to an EU region. For hosted, we maintain EU regions that keep data in-region. If regulations are stricter or you need on-prem, the Private option is available. There's more setup and licensing for Private.

[03:51] Marcelo: Performance-wise, we care about P95 for response generation. How do you typically hit 400ms P95?
[03:58] Darren: Depends on model size and token count. We optimize serving runtime with batching, KV cache, and attention kernels. For many workloads smaller open models in optimized configs can hit sub-200ms for short sequences; for longer responses or larger models latency increases. Also continuous batching can help but sometimes raises tail latency; we can tune batching and cache policies per route.

[04:26] Priya: Cost tradeoffs — can you share rough numbers comparing hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved capacity?
[04:33] Claire: Broadly, hosted is pay-as-you-go and is easier for PLG trials; per-token costs are higher at low volume but lower operational overhead. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model (monthly commit) and drives down per-token unit economics at scale. For the trial we usually recommend hosted credits. If you project sustained high qps, we can model committed capacity and show when dedicated pays off. We'll send a small ROI spreadsheet.

[04:59] Aisha: Any concerns about model versioning and rollouts? Our PMs want canary deploys and easy rollbacks.
[05:06] Darren: Redwood Console supports rollouts, canaries, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin production routes to a stable model; if a new variant degrades quality we can auto-fallback to a previous model. We'll demo that in an SE session if helpful.

[05:25] Marcelo: For the quickstart — what does the trial org include? Do we get sample prompts, evaluation harness, or usage dashboards?
[05:33] Claire: Trial org comes with free credits, a sample repo, pre-set dashboards for cost/latency, and a small eval harness you can run against your prompt set. We also include docs on quantization recommendations and batching tips to reduce cost.

[05:47] Priya: Who on your side will help with the benchmark? I want someone to run a realistic test that mimics our prompt shapes.
[05:53] Darren: That's me — I'll own the benchmark plan and run it with your team. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost, and throughput. We'll also test hosted first and if you want, run the same against a Dedicated config so you can compare.

[06:10] Aisha: About logs and auditability — are request/response bodies stored? We need to control retention and redaction for user PII.
[06:17] Claire: By default we retain logs for X days (we'll include exact retention numbers in the security doc), and you can configure retention windows. For Private customers you can fully control storage and retention. For hosted we have tools for redaction or skip storing user-specified fields. We'll include best practices in the documentation.

[06:36] Marcelo: Any hiccups folks typically hit in the first week?
[06:40] Darren: The usual is egress/firewall, tokenization surprises across model families, and not configuring batching properly which either wastes tokens or increases latency. Our runbook has those troubleshooting steps.

[06:53] Priya: If we like the hosted trial and then decide to move to Dedicated, how smooth is migration?
[06:59] Claire: Fairly straightforward — same API surface, same SDKs. You can pin model versions and we can help with the Dedicated capacity sizing and rollout. There may be a short window for data locality setup if you choose a Private migration.

[07:12] Aisha: Any red flags we should be aware of from a compliance perspective?
[07:16] Darren: Nothing unusual. For EU data residency, confirm region pins; for regulated PII, consider Private or strong contract terms on retention. We'll route to legal for any contract-specific clauses.

[07:29] Claire: Quick recap and proposed timeline — Claire creates trial org + credits by Friday; Priya shares traffic/latency targets by Thursday; Darren schedules a 60-minute SE benchmark next Tuesday; Aisha receives security docs today. Does that work?
[07:44] Priya: Yes works for us.
[07:46] Marcelo: Good.
[07:47] Aisha: Fine.

[07:49] Claire: Great. We'll follow up with email and the trial invite. Anything else before we close?
[07:55] Priya: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[07:58] Claire: Thanks, talk soon.

End notes: Shared artifacts during call: quickstart repo link (sent in chat), security pack (to be emailed), perf spreadsheet template (Darren).

Transcript end.
